days.topic: A day on Venus is longer than its year
days.hook: On Venus, a day is longer than a year.
days.facts: Venus rotates once every ~243 Earth days (sidereal) but orbits the Sun in ~225 days; it spins backwards (retrograde) so the Sun rises in the west; surface ~465°C, lead melts at 327°C. Do NOT claim sunrise-to-sunrise is 243 days (solar day is ~117 days).
days.title: A Day on Venus Is Longer Than Its Year 🤯 #shorts
days.note: Published early on Oct 29 as an end-to-end test.
days.style_idea: Bold type + spinning cube (claudevideo.org)

days.topic: Wombats poop cubes
days.hook: Wombats poop cubes.
days.facts: 80-100 cube-shaped droppings per night, ~2 cm; uneven elasticity of the intestine wall forms corners (Yang & Hu, Georgia Tech, 2018); cubes stack on rocks/logs and don't roll; 2019 Ig Nobel Prize in Physics.
days.title: Wombats Poop Cubes. Seriously. 🟫 #shorts
days.style_idea: Infrared night-vision trail camera: green-grey grain, REC/timestamp HUD, motion-detection boxes, ENHANCE zoom, time-lapse (wombats are nocturnal).

days.topic: The immortal jellyfish
days.hook: This jellyfish has figured out how to cheat death.
days.facts: Turritopsis dohrnii, ~4.5 mm; when stressed, injured or old it can revert from adult medusa to the polyp stage and grow up again; biologically 'immortal' in theory but most are eaten or die of disease.
days.title: This Jellyfish Can Reverse Its Own Life 🪼 #shorts
days.style_idea: Deep-sea bioluminescence: glowing translucent jellyfish with red core, marine snow, light shafts, VHS rewind when it turns back into a polyp.

days.topic: Sharks are older than trees
days.hook: Sharks have been around longer than trees.
days.facts: Earliest shark-like fish ~450 million years ago; earliest true trees (e.g. Archaeopteris / Wattieza) ~385-390 million years ago. Sharks also predate dinosaurs (~230 Mya).
days.style_idea: Deep-time rock strata: camera digs down through layered sandstone cross-sections; fossil silhouettes; earthy ochre palette; depth gauge in millions of years. Ref: 'Animated timeline of humanity…' (claudevideo.org).
days.title: Sharks Are Older Than Trees 🦈🌳 #shorts

days.topic: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid
days.hook: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
days.facts: Great Pyramid of Giza built ~2560 BC; Cleopatra VII lived 69-30 BC (~2,500 years later); Apollo 11 landed 1969 (~2,000 years after her).
days.title: Cleopatra Lived Closer to the Moon Landing Than the Pyramids ⏰ #shorts
days.note: Made in advance as the style sample; approved by the owner.
days.style_idea: One-day clock timeline (claudevideo.org)

days.topic: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood
days.hook: An octopus has three hearts. And its blood is blue.
days.facts: Two branchial hearts pump blood through the gills, one systemic heart to the body; the systemic heart stops beating while swimming; blood uses copper-based hemocyanin, making it blue.
days.title: An Octopus Has 3 Hearts and Blue Blood 🐙 #shorts
days.note: Made in advance as the style sample; approved by the owner.
days.style_idea: Paper-cutout (claudevideo.org)

days.topic: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire
days.hook: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
days.facts: Teaching at Oxford existed by 1096; Tenochtitlan was founded in 1325; the Aztec Triple Alliance formed 1428.
days.style_idea: Split screen: medieval illuminated manuscript (parchment, gold leaf initials, ink) vs flat-color codex-style glyph panels; pages turn. No sacred imagery. Ref: 'Jade-green Chinese landscape painting comes alive'.
days.title: Oxford Is Older Than the Aztec Empire 🤯 #shorts

days.topic: Bananas are berries, strawberries aren't
days.hook: Botanically, a banana is a berry. A strawberry is not.
days.facts: A botanical berry develops from a single flower with one ovary and has seeds inside (banana, tomato, grape); a strawberry is an 'accessory fruit' and its 'seeds' (achenes) are the actual fruits on the outside.
days.style_idea: Retro fruit-crate label printed in risograph: 2-3 spot colors, halftone dots, slight misregistration, paper texture; botanical cutaway of a banana. Ref: 'Claude Pop music video with a halftone portrait overlay'.
days.title: Bananas Are Berries. Strawberries Aren't. 🍌🍓 #shorts

days.topic: A teaspoon of neutron star weighs billions of tons
days.hook: One teaspoon of this star would weigh more than a mountain.
days.facts: Neutron stars pack more mass than the Sun into a sphere ~20 km across; a teaspoon of material would weigh on the order of billions of tons. Keep the figure as 'billions of tons'.
days.style_idea: Cinematic blue-white neutron star: spinning lighthouse beams, gravitational glow, volumetric haze, scale comparisons with a teaspoon and a mountain. Ref: 'Ray-traced black hole'. Must look different from the Saturn video (cold monochrome, no warm gold).
days.title: One Teaspoon of This Star Weighs BILLIONS of Tons ✨ #shorts

days.topic: More possible chess games than atoms in the universe
days.hook: There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
days.facts: Shannon number: ~10^120 possible chess games (a lower-bound estimate of game-tree complexity); atoms in the observable universe ~10^78-10^82.
days.style_idea: Isometric voxel chessboard; voxel pieces hop; counters explode into 10^120 vs 10^80 towers of tiny cubes. Ref: 'Voxel pelican rides a bike'.
days.title: More Chess Games Than Atoms in the Universe?! ♟️ #shorts

days.topic: Nintendo was founded in 1889 to sell playing cards
days.hook: The company behind Mario was founded in 1889. To sell playing cards.
days.facts: Nintendo was founded on 23 September 1889 in Kyoto by Fusajiro Yamauchi to make hanafuda playing cards. Same year the Eiffel Tower opened (1889). Do not show any Nintendo logos or characters.
days.style_idea: Japanese flower-card (hanafuda) art: bold red/black/cream cards, flat woodblock-print plants and moon, cards flip and deal; 1889 Kyoto. Generic cards only — no Nintendo logos, characters or products. Ref: 'Jade-green Chinese landscape painting comes alive'.
days.title: The Company Behind Mario Started in 1889 Selling CARDS 🎴 #shorts

days.topic: Days used to be shorter in the age of dinosaurs
days.hook: When dinosaurs were alive, a day didn't last 24 hours.
days.facts: Earth's rotation slows due to tidal friction from the Moon; ~70 million years ago a day was about 23.5 hours (study of fossil rudist shells, 2020).
days.style_idea: 16-bit pixel-art world: a dinosaur under a fast day/night cycle, pixel clock showing 23.5 h, scanlines. Ref: 'Pixel-art platformer where Clawd battles…'.
days.title: When Dinosaurs Lived, a Day WASN'T 24 Hours 🦕 #shorts

days.topic: Saturn would float in water
days.hook: Saturn is so light, it would float in a bathtub.
days.facts: Saturn's average density ~0.69 g/cm³, less than water's 1 g/cm³. Purely theoretical (no such bathtub; it's mostly gas).
days.title: Saturn Could Float in Water 🪐 #shorts
days.note: Made in advance as the style sample; approved by the owner.
days.style_idea: Glowing space / ray-traced look (claudevideo.org)

days.topic: Sloths can hold their breath for 40 minutes
days.hook: A sloth can hold its breath longer than a dolphin.
days.facts: Sloths can slow their heart rate and hold their breath up to ~40 minutes underwater; dolphins typically surface every ~8-10 minutes. They are surprisingly good swimmers.
days.style_idea: Soft claymation-look 3D rainforest: rounded pastel shapes, fingerprint texture, slow-motion pacing, sloth vs dolphin breath meters. Ref: 'Boxy orange mascot lives through a busy day'.
days.title: Sloths Can Hold Their Breath for 40 MINUTES 🦥 #shorts

days.topic: The Eiffel Tower grows in summer
days.hook: The Eiffel Tower gets taller every summer.
days.facts: Thermal expansion of iron: the tower can grow up to ~15 cm in heat and shrink in cold; it also tilts slightly away from the sun.
days.style_idea: Engineering blueprint: cyan grid, white line drawing of a lattice iron tower drawn stroke by stroke, dimension arrows, thermal expansion annotations. Ref: 'Turbofan jet engine opens into a 3D cutaway'.
days.title: The Eiffel Tower Gets TALLER Every Summer 🗼 #shorts

days.topic: Hippos make their own sunscreen
days.hook: Hippos sweat red. And it's sunscreen.
days.facts: Hippos secrete a reddish 'blood sweat' (not blood or sweat) containing hipposudoric and norhipposudoric acid that absorb UV light and may be antibacterial.
days.style_idea: 1960s magazine sunscreen ad: mid-century illustration, sun rays, cream paper, script + slab type, 'NEW! Hippo Formula' parody of a generic ad (no real brands). Ref: 'Motion promo for a game-asset generator'.
days.title: Hippos Sweat RED… and It's Sunscreen 🦛☀️ #shorts

days.topic: A planet where it rains glass sideways
days.hook: There's a planet where it rains glass. Sideways.
days.facts: Exoplanet HD 189733b, ~63 light-years away, a hot Jupiter; silicate particles in its atmosphere and winds ~8,700 km/h (~5,400 mph) suggest sideways 'glass rain'; its deep blue color was measured by Hubble (2013).
days.style_idea: Sci-fi interplanetary weather broadcast: HUD forecast UI, wind-speed dials, sideways glass-shard rain on a deep-blue planet. Ref: 'Frontier Lab Tycoon trailer with retro desktop UI'.
days.title: This Planet Rains Glass… SIDEWAYS 🌧️🪐 #shorts

days.topic: Scotland's national animal is the unicorn
days.hook: Scotland's national animal is a unicorn.
days.facts: The unicorn has been a Scottish heraldic symbol since the 12th-15th centuries (on the royal arms by the reign of James III); it represents purity and power, often shown chained.
days.style_idea: Heraldic tapestry: woven-thread texture, gold and navy, unicorn crest drawn like a coat of arms (generic, not the royal arms), banners unfurl.
days.title: Scotland's National Animal Is… a UNICORN 🦄 #shorts

days.topic: Butterflies taste with their feet
days.hook: Butterflies taste with their feet.
days.facts: Butterflies have chemoreceptors (taste sensors) on their feet/tarsi; females 'drum' on leaves to taste whether a plant is right for laying eggs.
days.style_idea: Naturalist's watercolor field journal: soft bleeding washes, pencil sketch lines, handwritten notes, a butterfly 'tasting' a leaf with its feet.

days.topic: Lightning is hotter than the Sun's surface
days.hook: A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
days.facts: Lightning can heat air to ~30,000 K (~27,000-30,000 °C), about five times hotter than the Sun's surface (~5,500 °C / ~5,800 K).
days.style_idea: Electric storm: dark cloud layers, procedurally branching lightning bolts, neon thermal scale comparing lightning vs the Sun's surface.

days.topic: A pineapple takes about two years to grow
days.hook: That pineapple took about two years to grow.
days.facts: A pineapple plant usually takes ~18-24 months to produce its first fruit, and each plant typically produces one fruit at a time.
days.style_idea: Tiny greenhouse diorama with tilt-shift look: a pineapple plant grows over a 24-month time-lapse calendar. Ref: 'Tropical island diorama with stilt huts'.

days.topic: Some turtles breathe through their butts
days.hook: Some turtles can breathe through their butts.
days.facts: Cloacal respiration: e.g. Australia's Fitzroy River turtle and white-throated snapping turtle absorb oxygen through their cloaca, letting them stay underwater for long periods.
days.style_idea: Family-friendly comic book: panels, halftone shading, speech bubbles, 'BLUB!' sound effects, a turtle doing its weird breathing trick underwater.

days.topic: The shortest war in history lasted under an hour
days.hook: The shortest war in history lasted less than an hour.
days.facts: Anglo-Zanzibar War, 27 August 1896, lasted roughly 38-45 minutes. Keep the tone light but factual; no graphic imagery.
days.style_idea: Vintage newspaper + 1890s newsreel: sepia, film scratches, headline typesetting, a stopwatch for the ~38–45 minute war; no graphic violence. Ref: 'Superintelligence documentary opens on an antique notebook'.

days.topic: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance
days.hook: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
days.facts: Collective noun 'flamboyance'; also flamingos are pink from carotenoid pigments in their diet (algae, brine shrimp), and are born grey/white.
days.style_idea: Pastel art-deco travel poster: geometric sunrays, flamingos as elegant flat shapes forming a 'flamboyance', gold line accents.

days.topic: Koalas have fingerprints like humans
days.hook: Koala fingerprints are so similar to ours, they could confuse a crime lab.
days.facts: Koala fingerprints are remarkably similar to human ones even under a microscope (Henneberg et al., 1996); evolved independently (convergent evolution).
days.style_idea: Forensic lab UI: fingerprint scans side by side (human vs koala), magnifier sweep, match-percentage meter, evidence board with string.

days.topic: The Moon is drifting away from Earth
days.hook: The Moon is running away from us.
days.facts: Lunar laser ranging (reflectors left by Apollo missions) shows the Moon recedes ~3.8 cm per year, about as fast as fingernails grow.
days.style_idea: 1970s space-mission print graphics: orange/brown/cream, mission-patch shapes, laser beam to the Moon's reflector, 3.8 cm/year ruler. No real agency logos.

days.topic: The mantis shrimp punch boils water
days.hook: This shrimp punches so fast, the water around it boils.
days.facts: Peacock mantis shrimp strike at ~23 m/s with huge acceleration, creating cavitation bubbles that collapse with flashes of light and briefly reach thousands of degrees; strong enough to break aquarium glass.
days.style_idea: Anime action: speed lines, impact frames, screen shake, a bubble collapsing with a flash of light, hand-drawn energy effects.

days.topic: Ancient Romans used urine to whiten teeth
days.hook: Ancient Romans brushed their teeth with urine.
days.facts: The ammonia in urine was used in Roman times for cleaning, laundry (fullonicae) and reportedly tooth whitening (mentioned by the poet Catullus); urine was valuable enough to be taxed under Vespasian.
days.style_idea: Roman floor mosaic: everything built from small stone tesserae that assemble and re-tile into each scene; terracotta, ochre, black, white.

days.topic: Tardigrades survived in open space
days.hook: This tiny animal survived the vacuum of space.
days.facts: Tardigrades (water bears, ~0.5 mm) survived exposure to space vacuum and cosmic radiation on the FOTON-M3 mission in 2007 by entering a dried-out 'tun' state.
days.style_idea: Microscope slide view: circular lens vignette, focus pulls, a tardigrade drawn as a scientific illustration, then a mission capsule. Ref: 'Proton collision inside a Large Hadron Collider detector'.

days.topic: Recap: the 5 weirdest facts of the month
days.hook: Thirty days of facts that sound fake. Here are the five weirdest.
days.facts: Quick-fire recap of five of the month's facts (pick the best performers in Metricool analytics if available), ending with a thank-you and follow call.
days.style_idea: Recap montage: each of the five weirdest facts shown in the style its own video used, cut to a beat, ending on the FAKE → TRUE switch.

days.topic: Honey never spoils
days.hook: Honey basically never goes bad.
days.facts: Honey's low water content and acidity stop bacteria; jars of honey thousands of years old found in Egyptian tombs reportedly still edible (Smithsonian Magazine).
days.style_idea: Golden honeycomb macro: hexagon cells filling with slow amber liquid, drips, warm backlight, ancient jar silhouette.
days.title: Honey Basically Never Goes Bad 🍯 #shorts
days.note: Tomb-tasting story is folklore; video only says honey was found in tombs.

days.topic: There are more trees on Earth than stars in our galaxy
days.hook: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
days.facts: ~3 trillion trees on Earth (Crowther et al., Nature 2015) vs roughly 100–400 billion stars in the Milky Way.
days.style_idea: Pointillism: thousands of colored dots that form a forest, then scatter into a galaxy; dots counted on screen.
days.title: More Trees on Earth Than Stars in Our Galaxy?! 🌳✨ #shorts

days.topic: Wood frogs freeze solid and come back to life
days.hook: This frog freezes solid every winter. Then it thaws and hops away.
days.facts: Wood frogs (Lithobates sylvaticus) survive freezing: heart stops, up to ~2/3 of body water freezes; glucose acts as antifreeze; they thaw in spring.
days.style_idea: Ice-crystal macro: frost ferns growing across the screen, cold blue palette, a frog frozen then thawing with a heartbeat restart.

days.title: This Frog FREEZES SOLID… Then Comes Back to Life 🐸🧊 #shorts

days.topic: Pluto hasn't finished one orbit since it was discovered
days.hook: Pluto hasn't finished a single lap around the Sun since we found it.
days.facts: Pluto discovered 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh; orbital period ~248 Earth years; first full orbit since discovery completes ~2178.
days.style_idea: 1930s astronomical glass photographic plates: negative star fields, blink-comparator flicker, handwritten plate labels.
days.title: Pluto Hasn't Finished ONE Orbit Since We Found It 🪐 #shorts

days.topic: Bubble wrap was invented as wallpaper
days.hook: Bubble wrap was supposed to be wallpaper.
days.facts: Invented 1957 by Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes as textured wallpaper; later used as packaging (Sealed Air founded 1960).
days.style_idea: 1960s mod wallpaper patterns: repeating bold motifs, then bubbles inflate and pop out of the pattern.
days.title: Bubble Wrap Was Supposed to Be WALLPAPER 🫧 #shorts

days.topic: Ketchup was once sold as medicine
days.hook: In the 1830s, ketchup was sold as medicine.
days.facts: In the 1830s Dr. John Cook Bennet promoted tomato ketchup as a remedy; 'tomato pills' were sold before being exposed as quackery (Smithsonian, Andrew F. Smith).
days.style_idea: Victorian apothecary label: engraved borders, ornate type, sepia paper, a bottle label being 'printed' layer by layer.
days.title: In the 1830s, Tomatoes Were Sold as MEDICINE 🍅 #shorts
days.note: Topic reframed from 'ketchup' to 'tomatoes' for accuracy.

days.topic: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep
days.hook: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep.
days.facts: Sea otters often hold paws or wrap in kelp while resting in groups ('rafts') to avoid drifting apart.
days.style_idea: Cozy felt and wool craft: fuzzy textures, stitched outlines, gentle bobbing on knitted waves.
days.title: Sea Otters Hold HANDS While They Sleep 🦦 #shorts

days.topic: A blue whale's heart is as big as a small car
days.hook: A blue whale's heart is about the size of a small car.
days.facts: Blue whale heart ~180 kg, roughly bumper-car sized (Canadian blue whale heart preserved by Royal Ontario Museum, 2015); heartbeat can drop to ~2 bpm while diving (Goldbogen et al., 2019).
days.style_idea: Natural-history museum infographic: scale silhouettes on cream, measuring lines, big heartbeat monitor slowing to 2 bpm.
days.title: A Blue Whale's Heart Is the Size of a BUMPER CAR 🐋 #shorts

days.topic: Crows can remember human faces
days.hook: Crows can remember your face. For years.
days.facts: University of Washington mask experiments (Marzluff): crows recognised a 'dangerous' mask years later and taught other crows.
days.style_idea: Film-noir detective: hard shadows, venetian-blind light, rain, typewriter case file on 'the masked suspect'.
days.title: Crows Remember Your FACE — For Years 🐦‍⬛ #shorts

days.topic: Hawaii is moving toward Japan
days.hook: Hawaii is slowly moving toward Japan.
days.facts: The Pacific Plate moves northwest about 7–10 cm per year, carrying Hawaii toward Japan.
days.style_idea: Topographic contour map: animated contour lines, plate arrows, a ruler showing cm per year over millions of years.
days.title: Hawaii Is Sliding Toward Japan… Right Now 🌋 #shorts

days.topic: Spider silk is stronger than steel, by weight
days.hook: Strand for strand, spider silk is stronger than steel.
days.facts: By weight, some spider dragline silk is stronger than steel and tougher than Kevlar.
days.style_idea: Macro photography look: dewy web at dawn, shallow depth of field, glistening droplets, a strand stretching under load.
days.title: Spider Silk Beats Steel… Pound for Pound 🕸️ #shorts

days.topic: Dolphins sleep with half their brain
days.hook: Dolphins sleep with one half of their brain at a time.
days.facts: Unihemispheric slow-wave sleep: one hemisphere sleeps while the other stays alert, one eye open; lets them surface to breathe.
days.style_idea: Split screen dreamscape: left half moonlit and dreamy, right half alert and crisp, a dolphin across the seam.
days.title: Dolphins Sleep With HALF Their Brain 🐬💤 #shorts

days.topic: Woolly mammoths were alive when the pyramids were built
days.hook: Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was built.
days.facts: Last mammoths survived on Wrangel Island until ~4,000 years ago (~2000 BC); Great Pyramid ~2560 BC.
days.style_idea: Cave painting: ochre and charcoal on rough rock, flickering torchlight, figures drawn stroke by stroke.

days.topic: There's enough gold in Earth's core to coat the planet
days.hook: There's enough gold in Earth's core to cover the whole planet.
days.facts: Estimates suggest enough gold in the core to coat Earth's surface ~0.5 m deep (Bernard Wood, Nature 2013).
days.style_idea: Molten gold: liquid metal reflections, cross-section of Earth with a glowing core, gold pouring over a globe.

days.topic: Antarctica is the biggest desert on Earth
days.hook: The biggest desert on Earth isn't hot. It's Antarctica.
days.facts: Deserts are defined by low precipitation; Antarctica (~14 million km²) gets very little and is the largest desert, larger than the Sahara.
days.style_idea: Minimal polar design: white on white, subtle snow shading, thin blue lines, wind particles, sparse elegant type.

days.topic: Hummingbirds can fly backwards
days.hook: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can truly fly backwards.
days.facts: Hummingbirds can hover and fly backwards; wings beat dozens of times per second (up to ~80 in small species).
days.style_idea: Eadweard Muybridge-style motion study: sequential photo frames in a grid, sepia, frame numbers, stroboscopic wing positions.

days.topic: Astronauts get taller in space
days.hook: Astronauts get taller in space.
days.facts: Without gravity compressing the spine, astronauts can grow up to ~3% taller (NASA); it reverses back on Earth.
days.style_idea: Playful zero-gravity UI: floating rounded panels, drifting objects, soft pastel space station interior, a height scale.

days.topic: Sound travels faster in water than in air
days.hook: Sound moves about four times faster in water than in air.
days.facts: Speed of sound ~343 m/s in air (20°C) vs ~1,480 m/s in fresh water.
days.style_idea: Retro oscilloscope: phosphor-green waveforms on a CRT grid, knobs, waves racing between two lanes (air vs water).

days.topic: The Great Pyramid was the tallest building for 3,800 years
days.hook: For about 3,800 years, the tallest building on Earth was the Great Pyramid.
days.facts: At ~146 m the Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure until Lincoln Cathedral's spire (~1311 AD).
days.style_idea: Carved stone relief: sandstone texture, chiselled reveal of shapes and numbers, low raking light.

days.topic: Glass frogs have see-through skin
days.hook: You can see this frog's heart beating through its skin.
days.facts: Glass frogs (Centrolenidae) have translucent belly skin showing organs; at rest they can hide most of their red blood cells in the liver to become more transparent (Science, 2022).
days.style_idea: X-ray/transparency look: dark background, glowing translucent layers, a scanner sweep revealing organs and a beating heart.

days.topic: Polar bears have black skin
days.hook: Under that white fur, a polar bear's skin is black.
days.facts: Polar bear skin is black; fur hairs are translucent/hollow and look white by scattering light.
days.style_idea: Thermal camera palette (purple-orange-yellow): heat map of an icy scene, a polar bear silhouette, fur 'turning' transparent.

days.topic: Some bamboo can grow almost a meter in a day
days.hook: Some bamboo can grow almost a meter in a single day.
days.facts: Some bamboo species can grow up to ~91 cm (35 in) in 24 hours (Guinness World Records).
days.style_idea: Zen ink brush painting: sumi-e strokes on rice paper, bamboo growing segment by segment, red seal stamp.

days.topic: A fluffy cloud can weigh as much as 100 elephants
days.hook: That fluffy cloud weighs about as much as a hundred elephants.
days.facts: USGS: a typical cumulus cloud holds ~500 tonnes (≈1.1 million lb) of water; an elephant ~5–6 tonnes.
days.style_idea: Dreamy watercolor sky: soft bleeding washes, paper grain, elephants drawn as clouds drifting, a hanging scale.

days.topic: Honeybees dance to give directions
days.hook: Honeybees dance to tell each other where food is.
days.facts: The waggle dance encodes direction (angle to the sun) and distance (waggle duration) — Karl von Frisch, Nobel Prize 1973.
days.style_idea: Bauhaus geometry: primary colors, circles/triangles/lines, the dance path drawn as a geometric diagram with the sun angle.

days.topic: Titan has rain, rivers and lakes — of methane
days.hook: On Saturn's moon Titan, it rains. But not water.
days.facts: Titan has methane/ethane rain, rivers and lakes (Cassini–Huygens); surface ~-179°C.
days.style_idea: 1950s pulp sci-fi magazine cover: painterly orange skies, bold retro lettering, halftone, rocket-age drama (no real titles).

days.topic: Chickens are close relatives of T. rex
days.hook: The closest living relatives of T. rex include… chickens.
days.facts: Birds are living dinosaurs; 2007–2008 T. rex collagen protein studies found its closest match among living animals in chickens and ostriches.
days.style_idea: Museum blackboard chalk drawings: skeletons sketched in chalk, dust, arrows morphing a T. rex skeleton into a chicken.
